items.title: 68642_Jo Jones oral history interview
items.q: Before he could open his mouth I said, "You're going to play Radio City."

ctx.x: Sticks Evans is another percussionist, young percussionist.

I said, "You will not - you are a percussionist." The first time he ran to me and said, "Guess what?" I said, "What are you talking about?" Before he could open his mouth I said, "You're going to play Radio City." He said, "How do you know?" I said, "They're friends of mine." Naturally I was hanging out with Mr. Billy Gladstone and the people at Radio City - that's Wall Street and Mr. Billy Gladstone would

sit and look and hear guys play and he already knew he was the epitome. He was such a flexible man, you see. He knew the peoples that I knew from living in Washington - he knew the Johnsons, he knew the peoples. That's the reason he could understand me. I knew the Chick Webbs and Sid Catletts and what have you, but to know these peoples and to have that background, you see. It was something different, Milt.
